title.narrative: Emergency response to flood affected victims in El Jabalein town, El Jabalein locality, White Nile

description.narrative:
White Nile State has reportedly received more than expected rains, which has resulted to occurrence of flash floods. El Jabalein locality has received very heavy rains (continuous one between 31st of July and 2nd of August in El Jabalein town) which resulted to flash floods that led to destruction of property, displacement of people, and at least three people reported to have been wounded. The rains have since subsided, but it is not certain whether more rains will be received. An inter-agency rapid needs assessment was conducted on 1st August focusing on the worst affected area (13 blocks within El Jabalein town) and established that: a). 471 houses were damaged (419 completely and 52 partially), thus the 471 households require shelter support. b). 3 persons were wounded. c). 471 households are in urgent need of safe drinking water, jerrycans for storage of water, soap, blankets, plastic sheets, mats, mosquito nets, and food d). Affected households have received 240 plastic sheets (provided by Civil Defence), and vector control materials (provided by MoH).
CAFOD (in partnership with SIDO) is proposing to intervene in the crisis by supporting the most affected families (200 HHs, giving preference to households with pregnant and lactating women, female/child headed households, households with members who are elderly and disabled) by providing them with blankets, soap, water jerrycans, mats and mosquito nets and plastic sheets. From the needs assessment, the affected communities prioritised the mentioned NFIs as of great necessity to them, given that what they had, had been washed away or submerged under the water, together with their collapsed houses. Part of the affected population have already received plastic sheets for make-shift shelters. The support will be delivered in close collaboration with other partners to minimise duplication and double-support.
